title: Homework: reopen the crosswind claim
brief: Review a changed crosswind requirement through twelve connected sections. Start with the mission briefing below.

fields.label: Changed crosswind engineering question
fields.help: Ask whether the aircraft can meet the changed crosswind requirement. State the 6 m/s crosswind and distinguish the local yaw calculation from a landing decision.

fields.label: Local rudder balance: deltaR = (use CnBeta, beta, Cn0, CnRudder)
fields.help: Rearrange CnBeta*beta + CnRudder*deltaR + Cn0 = 0 for deltaR. Enter only the expression using the named variables.

fields.label: Synthetic sideslip beta (rad)
fields.help: Enter the independently supplied sideslip angle in radians. Do not convert the crab heading into sideslip. Enter a number only.

fields.help: Choose the question the supplied steady yaw equation can answer by itself.

fields.label: Predicted rudder-deflection ratio if beta doubles
fields.help: Predict new rudder deflection divided by original deflection if sideslip doubles and Cn0 remains zero. Enter a number only.

fields.label: Local rudder demand at beta=0.08 rad (rad)
fields.help: Calculate deltaR by hand for beta=0.08 rad. Enter radians with the correct sign and show the working below. Enter a number only.

fields.label: Behavior when CnRudder=0
fields.help: If CnRudder=0, the rudder has no modeled effect on yaw. Choose how the calculation should handle this input.

optionLabels.Reject ineffective local balance: Reject the input: the model gives the rudder no yaw effect

fields.label: Result when roll/gust/ground-contact evidence is missing
fields.help: Choose what the app should report about a crosswind landing when it has only a steady yaw equation.

fields.label: JavaScript: function calculate(input) returning rudder demand (rad)
fields.help: Paste a JavaScript function named calculate(input). Return a number; do not paste Markdown fences or terminal commands.

checks.message: The supplied synthetic local yaw balance requires +0.1 rad rudder.
Use radians and preserve the declared positive sideslip.

checks.expected: Coupled yaw, roll, lateral force and transient limits
checks.message: A yaw-only calculation cannot establish the operational claim.
Do not present the teaching values as aircraft evidence.
Keep the local balance separate from landing safety.
With Cn0=0, the local rudder demand scales linearly with beta.
Show the independent signed balance calculation.
Division by zero effectiveness is not a valid control solution.
Missing coupled evidence must remain visible.

checks.expected: Withhold crosswind claim pending coupled evidence
checks.message: The earlier pitch calculation does not answer the changed roll/yaw requirement.

hints: The 16.7° crab angle is a wind-triangle heading offset, not rudder deflection or the synthetic beta.
Solve the signed local yaw balance: deltaR=-(CnBeta*beta+Cn0)/CnRudder. Check both sides of the travel range.
Even a passing local yaw/travel case cannot establish the combined motions and forces of a crosswind landing. Withhold that claim and identify the next evidence.

sweep.units: Synthetic sideslip beta and signed rudder demand in rad. Positive travel limit +0.12 rad shown; negative limit is -0.12 rad.

codeCases.label: Doubled sideslip demands twice the rudder

codeContract.description: Implement calculate(input) returning -(CnBeta*beta+Cn0)/CnRudder in rad. Require finite numeric inputs and nonzero CnRudder. Throw Error for invalid inputs. This local yaw balance cannot establish crosswind controllability.

experience.scenario: The trainer now faces a 6 m/s crosswind at 20 m/s runway-axis airspeed. Wind-triangle geometry gives a 16.7° crab heading offset. This is not rudder deflection or sideslip.
experience.task: Complete all twelve sections using the scenario and synthetic local balance below. Keep the local calculation separate from the operational crosswind decision.
experience.method: For the local teaching exercise only: CnBeta=0.10/rad, beta=0.08 rad, Cn0=0, CnRudder=−0.08/rad, rudder limits ±0.12 rad. Balance CnBeta×beta + CnRudder×deltaR + Cn0 = 0. The beta value is an independent sideslip scenario, not converted crab angle. No roll, lateral force, gust, de-crab, tire, clearance or workload model is supplied.
experience.investigate: Inspect baseline, doubled and reversed sideslip using your actual code. Record signed travel sufficiency, then identify missing evidence and consequences before deciding the claim about aircraft operation.
experience.tools: Use the built-in JavaScript editor. An existing coding assistant is optional.

variableKey.usableLimit: Signed rudder limit magnitude (rad); applies in both directions

reflection.included: Your code checks a local yaw-moment balance and signed rudder travel for specified sideslip values.
reflection.omitted: It does not simulate a gust, the time taken to respond, coupled roll motion or a crosswind landing.
reflection.question: Before accepting a crosswind operating limit, which missing test or model would you investigate first, and why?
reflection.help: Use one specific detail from this investigation. Explain what you would check next and why it matters; you do not need to perform that new test here.

experience.terms: Crab is heading offset used to counter wind drift. Sideslip β is the angle between the aircraft’s forward axis and its air-relative motion. Rudder deflection δR is a control angle. They are different quantities. Synthetic means invented for this teaching exercise, not aircraft test data.

cases.label: Synthetic local yaw reference
cases.prompt: Compare the signed rudder angle with the −0.12 to +0.12 rad range. Explain whether it fits, and how reversing sideslip affects the required direction.
cases.interpretationHint: Compare the magnitude of your executed rudder demand with 0.12 rad in either direction.
